name: sprintf_string
expr: s1 = sprintf('%s', "hello"); n1 = numel(s1); c1 = double(s1(1)); c5 = double(s1(5)); s2 = sprintf('%s-%s', "ab", "cd"); n2 = numel(s2); c2 = double(s2(3)); s3 = sprintf('%s', ["x" "yz"]); n3 = numel(s3); c3a = double(s3(1)); c3c = double(s3(3)); s4 = sprintf('%s=%d', "k", 7); n4 = numel(s4); c4 = double(s4(3));
comment: sprintf/fprintf %s with the string type vs MATLAB R2025b. Bug fixed 2026-05-30: %s only accepted char arrays, so a string scalar printed nothing (fprintf('%s',"hi") -> empty). Now %s prints string scalars (s1='hello', n1=5) and cycles the format over a string array's elements like MATLAB (sprintf('%s',["x" "yz"])='xyz', n3=3). Mixed string+numeric specs also work (s4='k=7'). NOTE: double-quoted string literals require the string type; no semicolons inside quoted strings.
